players.product: Power and distribution transformers and substations (T&D) for grid connection, plus Marathon alternators for data-center energy backup and industrial pumps / ventilation equipment for cooling systems

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 (CFO Andre Luis Rodrigues): net operating revenue returned to growth, up 5.7% versus Q3 2025; international revenue was 62.5% of total, the highest level ever, with another quarter of double-digit growth in U.S. dollars; EBITDA BRL 2.3 billion, up 3.1%, with the EBITDA margin 'closing the quarter at 21%' (IR director Andre Salgueiro later cited 21.6%, as spoken); ROIC up 0.8 percentage points to 33.2%. Nine-month EBITDA margin 20.9% versus 20% in 2025 (Rodrigues). In Brazil growth resumed on long-cycle deliveries (T&D, automation systems for pulp and paper) despite weaker short-cycle demand and no utility-scale solar projects. Salgueiro: international GTD growth came mostly from generators (Marathon) rather than T&D; T&D is two-thirds of that international business.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue +5.7% YoY; international 62.5% of revenue; EBITDA BRL 2.3 billion (+3.1%); ROIC 33.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (IR director Andre Salgueiro / CFO Andre Luis Rodrigues): the expanded Betim plant began operating in the quarter, adding large power transformer capacity, and the T&D business should grow faster with it; the Mexico and Colombia transformer greenfields come into operation in the first quarter of 2027, with highly specialized teams hired and trained since the beginning of the year; an expansion of the Gravatai plant follows next year. Q3 capex was BRL 905 million (40% Brazil, 60% abroad): T&D capacity, Jaragua do Sul and Guaramirim, vertical integration in Linhares, transformer plants in Mexico, Colombia and the U.S., and high-voltage motor capacity in China.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 capex BRL 905 million; Mexico and Colombia transformer plants operational Q1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: New investments (IR director Andre Salgueiro): in September WEG announced a new investment of approximately BRL 840 million to expand generation production capacity in North America, aimed at power generation for critical applications in the U.S., 'particularly driven by the expansion of data centers'; it also expanded its battery energy storage systems plant under construction in Itajai, Santa Catarina, to total estimated investment of BRL 330 million and annual capacity of four gigawatt-hours, expected ready in the second half of next year. WEG is focused on Brazil's BESS auction set for the beginning of December (volumes and rules not yet disclosed) and says the auction could make a significant contribution in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: BRL 840 million North American generator capacity; BESS plant BRL 330 million, 4 GWh per year, ready H2 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers (IR director Andre Salgueiro): international short-cycle demand was positive in oil and gas, mining and 'ventilation cooling systems for data center segments', and the Marathon generator business performed strongly 'supplying backup power generation for data centers'; cooling for data centers 'practically doubled vis-a-vis last year, with a very positive dynamic going forward'. Ventilation motors are sold 65% to 70% through OEMs, so the end customer is not always known. Marathon margins are 'somewhat below' WEG's average but improved quarter on quarter. International orders were strong, 'building a healthy order backlog for the coming quarters'.
quarterly_data.figure: data-center cooling business practically doubled year on year; 65% to 70% of ventilation sales through OEMs

quarterly_data.signal: Costs and margins (CFO Andre Luis Rodrigues / IR director Andre Salgueiro): comparing September 2025 with September 2026 in the international market, copper rose 40% and steel more than 20%; Section 232 tariffs now apply to transformers exported from Mexico to the U.S.; pre-operational personnel costs for plants under construction and higher freight weigh on margins, partly mitigated by long-term freight contracts and price pass-through over time. The U.S. tariff reimbursement process is under way in tranches over a period; the Q3 amount was immaterial.
quarterly_data.figure: copper +40%, steel more than 20% (September 2026 vs September 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (IR director Andre Salgueiro / CFO Andre Luis Rodrigues): WEG remains confident in 'a favorable environment for continued revenue growth', but raw material costs could pressure operating margins. In Brazil every business except paints and varnishes retracted in the quarter on high interest rates and the electoral environment, and 'our backlog is one or two months ahead', so Q4 and 2027 must be watched; domestic T&D growth should accelerate with the new capacity, and thermal and hydro generation and energy storage contribute positively.
